cards.hypothesis: Inter-subject variability in autonomic nervous system dynamics causes conformal prediction coverage to degrade for subjects with high heart rate variability during non-stationary segments
cards.proposed_mechanism: Subjects with high baseline heart rate variability (HRV) exhibit greater non-stationarity in RR interval distributions during physiological state transitions, violating the exchangeability assumption of conformal prediction and causing prediction intervals to undercover during transition segments
cards.causal_path: High baseline HRV (RMSSD > 50ms) -> Increased non-stationarity during state transitions (quantified by sliding-window KL divergence > 0.3) -> Violation of exchangeability assumption -> Conformal prediction interval undercoverage (empirical coverage < 1-alpha - 0.05)
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage instability is driven by signal noise floor differences across subjects rather than autonomic dynamics
cards.rival_prediction: Subjects with low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR < 10dB) show coverage degradation regardless of HRV level
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare coverage stability in high-HRV/high-SNR vs low-HRV/low-SNR subjects; mechanism predicts high-HRV drives instability even with high SNR
cards.effect_size_rationale: Prior work shows HRV correlates with non-stationarity magnitude (r~0.4-0.6); conformal coverage drops of 5-15% observed in non-stationary settings
minimum_data_needed: simultaneous respiration or activity labels for state transition identification
cards.testable_prediction: Empirical coverage during high-KL-divergence segments will be at least 5 percentage points below nominal for high-HRV subjects (RMSSD>50ms) but within 2 points for low-HRV subjects
cards.failure_condition: No significant difference in coverage degradation between high-HRV and low-HRV subjects during high-KL-divergence segments (p>0.05, paired test)
cards.statistical_test_plan: Linear mixed model: coverage_gap ~ HRV_group * KL_divergence_bin + (1|subject) + age + SNR; test interaction term
cards.falsification_test: Induce artificial non-stationarity via synthetic distribution shifts in low-HRV subjects' data; if coverage remains stable, mechanism is falsified because non-stationarity alone doesn't explain the effect

cards.hypothesis: Sensor electrode-skin impedance drift during long recordings causes progressive miscalibration of conformal prediction intervals specifically in segments with high motion artifact density
cards.proposed_mechanism: Increasing electrode-skin impedance alters the amplitude distribution of ECG signals, which shifts the residual distribution of the underlying predictor; conformal prediction calibrated on early low-impedance segments produces intervals that are too narrow for later high-impedance segments with motion artifacts
cards.causal_path: Electrode-skin impedance increase (>20% from baseline) -> ECG amplitude attenuation and baseline wander -> Increased predictor residual variance in motion-contaminated segments -> Conformal quantile underestimation -> Coverage below nominal
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage degradation is caused by physiological non-stationarity that coincidentally correlates with recording duration
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage drops equally in clean and motion-contaminated segments as recording progresses
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare coverage trajectories in high-motion vs low-motion segments; mechanism predicts divergence only in high-motion segments
cards.effect_size_rationale: Impedance changes of 20-50% are common in >30min recordings; motion artifacts amplify residual variance 2-3x; conformal quantiles can underestimate by 30-50% under distribution shift
minimum_data_needed: Ground truth labels for prediction task
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage in high-motion segments (artifact density >15%) will decline by >10 percentage points over 60min while low-motion segments remain within 3 points of nominal
cards.failure_condition: Coverage decline is similar magnitude in high-motion and low-motion segments (difference <3 percentage points)
cards.statistical_test_plan: Segmented regression with breakpoint at impedance threshold; test slope difference between high/low motion segments using bootstrap CI
cards.falsification_test: Re-calibrate conformal predictor every 10min using only recent data; if coverage stabilizes, the mechanism (static calibration on drifting distribution) is confirmed; if coverage still degrades, mechanism is falsified

cards.hypothesis: Circadian variation in QT interval dynamics violates the exchangeability assumption when conformal prediction is trained on daytime data but applied to nighttime segments
cards.proposed_mechanism: QT-RR hysteresis and circadian autonomic shifts cause the conditional distribution of QT given RR to differ systematically between day and night; conformal prediction intervals calibrated on pooled data achieve nominal coverage overall but undercover specifically in nighttime segments due to unmodeled distributional shift
cards.causal_path: Circadian phase (melatonin onset) -> Autonomic balance shift (LF/HF ratio decrease >30%) -> Altered QT-RR relationship (hysteresis loop area change >20%) -> Conditional distribution shift P(QT|RR) -> Conformal prediction interval miscalibration in night segments
cards.rival_explanation: Nighttime coverage drop is due to increased motion artifacts during sleep rather than circadian physiology
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage degradation correlates with actigraphy-measured movement, not circadian phase
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare coverage in quiet wakefulness at night vs daytime; mechanism predicts nighttime degradation persists without motion
cards.effect_size_rationale: QT-RR hysteresis changes of 15-25% documented across circadian cycle; conformal coverage gaps of 5-10% observed under conditional distribution shift
cards.testable_prediction: Nighttime segments (2-6h post-DLMO) will show coverage 5-10 percentage points below nominal while daytime segments maintain nominal coverage, after controlling for motion
cards.failure_condition: No significant coverage difference between circadian phases after adjusting for motion artifact density (p>0.05)
cards.statistical_test_plan: Generalized additive model: coverage ~ s(circadian_phase) + motion_density + (1|subject); test significance of smooth term
cards.falsification_test: Train separate conformal predictors for day and night segments; if both achieve nominal coverage within their domains, the mechanism (single predictor across phases) is confirmed; if nighttime predictor still undercovers, mechanism is falsified

cards.hypothesis: Inconsistent R-peak annotation quality across physiological segments introduces label noise that differentially biases conformal prediction residuals
cards.proposed_mechanism: Automated R-peak detectors have lower sensitivity during high-motion or arrhythmic segments, causing systematic under-detection of beats; this creates a segment-dependent label noise pattern where residual distributions become skewed, violating the symmetry assumption of split conformal prediction
cards.causal_path: Segment type (motion/arrhythmia) -> R-peak detection sensitivity drop (>10% below baseline) -> Systematic label omission -> Asymmetric residual distribution (skewness >1.5) -> Split conformal prediction interval asymmetry -> Conditional coverage violation
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage instability stems from true physiological variability in the prediction target, not annotation errors
cards.rival_prediction: Residual distributions remain symmetric (skewness <0.5) even in segments with coverage degradation
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare residual skewness and coverage in segments with manually verified vs automated annotations; mechanism predicts skewness only in automated
cards.effect_size_rationale: R-peak detection sensitivity drops 10-30% in motion/arrhythmia; skewness >1.5 can cause 5-15% conditional coverage violations in split conformal
minimum_data_needed: ECG with expert-verified R-peak annotations for >=100 segments
cards.testable_prediction: Segments with detection sensitivity <90% will show residual skewness >1.5 and conditional coverage deviation >5% from nominal, while verified segments maintain symmetry and coverage
cards.failure_condition: Residual skewness <0.5 in low-sensitivity segments, or coverage deviation <2% despite high skewness
cards.statistical_test_plan: Quantile regression of coverage_gap on detection_sensitivity and skewness; test if skewness mediates the sensitivity-coverage relationship (Sobel test)
cards.falsification_test: Replace automated annotations with expert annotations in low-sensitivity segments and re-run conformal prediction; if coverage stabilizes, mechanism confirmed; if coverage remains unstable, mechanism falsified

cards.hypothesis: Improper stratification by physiological state during calibration causes conformal prediction to undercover during rare but critical states (e.g., atrial fibrillation episodes)
cards.proposed_mechanism: Standard conformal prediction calibrates on pooled data dominated by normal sinus rhythm; the resulting prediction intervals are too narrow for rare states with higher residual variance (e.g., AFib), causing severe undercoverage specifically during those clinically critical segments
cards.causal_path: Rare state prevalence (<5% of data) -> Pooled calibration quantile dominated by common state -> Prediction interval width insufficient for rare state residual variance -> Rare state coverage << nominal (e.g., <70% at 90% nominal)
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage in rare states is due to inherent unpredictability of those states, not calibration strategy
cards.rival_prediction: Even state-specific conformal predictors (trained only on that state) fail to achieve nominal coverage for rare states
cards.distinguishing_test: Train state-stratified conformal predictors; mechanism predicts rare-state coverage recovers to nominal with stratified calibration
cards.effect_size_rationale: AFib residual variance can be 3-5x sinus rhythm; pooled 90% quantile may cover only 60-70% of AFib residuals; stratified calibration should recover to ~90%
minimum_data_needed: ECG with beat-level rhythm annotations (sinus, AFib, other)
cards.testable_prediction: Pooled conformal coverage during AFib segments <75% at 90% nominal; state-stratified conformal coverage during AFib 85-95%
cards.failure_condition: State-stratified conformal coverage for AFib remains <80% at 90% nominal
cards.statistical_test_plan: McNemar's test comparing coverage indicator (covered/not) between pooled and stratified methods within AFib segments; binomial test for nominal coverage achievement
cards.falsification_test: Generate synthetic data where rare state has same residual distribution as common state; if pooled conformal still undercovers rare state, mechanism falsified (it's a prevalence artifact, not variance difference)

cards.hypothesis: Temporal autocorrelation in prediction residuals violates the i.i.d. assumption of conformal prediction, causing coverage to degrade during prolonged physiological states
cards.proposed_mechanism: Physiological signals exhibit long-range temporal correlations (Hurst exponent H>0.7); prediction residuals inherit this autocorrelation, causing consecutive residuals to be similar. Conformal prediction assumes exchangeability, so during prolonged states the effective sample size for calibration is much smaller than nominal, leading to quantile estimation error and coverage instability
cards.causal_path: Long-range temporal correlation in physiology (Hurst H>0.7) -> Autocorrelated predictor residuals (lag-1 ACF >0.5) -> Reduced effective calibration sample size (n_eff << n) -> Conformal quantile estimation variance inflation -> Coverage oscillation around nominal with period matching state duration
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage instability is due to non-stationary mean shifts, not autocorrelation
cards.rival_prediction: Residuals show mean shifts but low autocorrelation (lag-1 ACF <0.2) during unstable coverage periods
cards.distinguishing_test: Compute effective sample size from residual ACF; mechanism predicts n_eff/n <0.3 correlates with coverage instability
cards.effect_size_rationale: Physiological signals show H=0.7-0.9; n_eff can be 5-10x smaller than n; conformal quantile variance scales with 1/n_eff causing coverage std dev of 3-8%
cards.testable_prediction: Segments with residual lag-1 ACF >0.5 will show coverage standard deviation >5% across bootstrap resamples, while segments with ACF <0.2 show <2%
cards.failure_condition: No correlation between residual ACF and coverage instability (Spearman rho <0.2, p>0.05)
cards.statistical_test_plan: Bootstrap conformal quantile estimation 1000x per segment; regress coverage_std on residual_ACF using beta regression; test slope significance
cards.falsification_test: Apply block conformal prediction with block size matched to autocorrelation decay; if coverage stabilizes, mechanism confirmed; if instability persists, mechanism falsified

cards.hypothesis: Respiratory sinus arrhythmia amplitude modulation creates periodic coverage oscillations in conformal prediction for RR interval forecasting
cards.proposed_mechanism: RSA causes cyclic variation in RR interval predictability (high predictability at end-expiration, low at end-inspiration); conformal prediction calibrated on full respiratory cycles produces intervals that are too wide during high-predictability phases and too narrow during low-predictability phases, creating periodic coverage oscillations
cards.causal_path: Respiratory phase (inspiration/expiration) -> RSA amplitude (peak-trough RR difference) -> Conditional residual variance modulation (expiration variance < inspiration variance) -> Fixed conformal quantile mismatch -> Periodic coverage oscillation (expiration coverage > nominal, inspiration coverage < nominal)
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage oscillations are caused by cardiac cycle length effects, not respiratory modulation
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage oscillates at heart rate frequency (~1Hz), not respiratory frequency (~0.25Hz)
cards.distinguishing_test: Spectral analysis of coverage time series; mechanism predicts peak at respiratory frequency, rival predicts peak at cardiac frequency
cards.effect_size_rationale: RSA amplitude 20-100ms; residual variance ratio inspiration/expiration ~1.5-2x; coverage oscillation amplitude ~3-8% at 90% nominal
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage during expiration phases will exceed nominal by 3-8%; coverage during inspiration will fall below nominal by 3-8%; oscillation frequency matches respiratory rate
cards.failure_condition: No significant coverage difference between respiratory phases (paired t-test p>0.05) or oscillation frequency != respiratory frequency
cards.statistical_test_plan: Circular-linear regression: coverage ~ sin(respiratory_phase) + cos(respiratory_phase); test amplitude significance via permutation test
cards.falsification_test: Stratify calibration by respiratory phase (inspiration vs expiration); if phase-stratified conformal eliminates oscillations, mechanism confirmed; if oscillations persist, mechanism falsified

cards.hypothesis: Non-exchangeability induced by abrupt physiological state transitions (e.g., sleep stage changes) causes conformal prediction to fail specifically at transition boundaries
cards.proposed_mechanism: Sleep stage transitions (e.g., NREM to REM) create abrupt distributional shifts in HRV features; conformal prediction calibrated on pre-transition data produces intervals that fail to cover post-transition residuals because the calibration set contains no examples from the new regime
cards.causal_path: Sleep stage transition (hypnogram change) -> Abrupt HRV feature distribution shift (Wasserstein distance >0.5) -> Calibration set lacks post-transition examples -> Conformal quantile based on pre-transition residuals -> Transition boundary coverage collapse (<50% at 90% nominal)
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage drop at transitions is due to movement artifacts during body position changes, not physiological state change
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage drops only at transitions accompanied by actigraphy movement >threshold
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare coverage at spontaneous transitions without movement vs movement-matched non-transition periods
cards.effect_size_rationale: Sleep stage transitions cause HRV distribution shifts (Wasserstein >0.5); conformal coverage at boundaries can drop to 40-60% at 90% nominal in similar regime-shift settings
minimum_data_needed: Overnight PSG with ECG and hypnogram
>=30 subjects with >=5 clear stage transitions each
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage in 60s windows centered on stage transitions <60% at 90% nominal; coverage in matched steady-state windows >85%
cards.failure_condition: Transition boundary coverage >80% at 90% nominal, or no difference from steady-state
cards.statistical_test_plan: Generalized estimating equations: coverage_indicator ~ transition_window + (1|subject); test transition_window coefficient
cards.falsification_test: Use online conformal prediction with adaptive calibration window (only post-transition data); if coverage recovers at boundaries, mechanism confirmed; if not, mechanism falsified

cards.hypothesis: Conformal prediction coverage fails during ectopic beat sequences because the predictor's error distribution becomes bimodal, violating the unimodal assumption of quantile estimation
cards.proposed_mechanism: Ectopic beats (PVCs/PACs) create a mixture residual distribution: correctly predicted sinus beats (low error) and mispredicted ectopic beats (high error). The conformal quantile estimated from this mixture falls in the valley between modes, causing simultaneous overcoverage for sinus beats and undercoverage for ectopic beats
cards.causal_path: Ectopic beat density >10% -> Bimodal residual distribution (Hartigan's dip test p<0.01) -> Conformal quantile falls between modes -> Sinus beat coverage > nominal + 10%, ectopic beat coverage < nominal - 20%
cards.rival_explanation: Ectopic beats simply have higher variance but unimodal residuals; conformal quantile appropriately covers the mixture
cards.rival_prediction: Residual distribution passes unimodality test (dip test p>0.05) even at high ectopic density
cards.distinguishing_test: Test residual distribution unimodality separately for high-ectopic vs low-ectopic segments
cards.effect_size_rationale: Ectopic prediction errors can be 5-10x sinus errors; bimodal mixtures cause quantile estimation bias of 20-40% coverage gap between components
minimum_data_needed: ECG with beat-type annotations (sinus, PVC, PAC)
cards.testable_prediction: At ectopic density >15%, residual dip test p<0.01; sinus beat coverage >95% at 90% nominal; ectopic beat coverage <70%
cards.failure_condition: Residual distribution unimodal (dip test p>0.05) at high ectopic density, or ectopic beat coverage >80%
cards.statistical_test_plan: Hartigan's dip test for unimodality per segment; beta-binomial regression for coverage by beat type; interaction test ectopic_density * beat_type
cards.falsification_test: Train separate conformal predictors for sinus and ectopic beats (using morphology features); if both achieve nominal coverage, mechanism confirmed; if ectopic predictor still undercovers, mechanism falsified

cards.hypothesis: Finite-sample conformal prediction coverage guarantees fail when calibration set size per physiological stratum is below the threshold required for valid quantile estimation
cards.proposed_mechanism: When data is stratified by physiological state (e.g., 5 sleep stages x 4 activity levels = 20 strata), some strata have very few calibration points (n<30). The conformal quantile estimator has high variance at small n, causing coverage to randomly fluctuate above/below nominal across strata, creating apparent instability that is actually estimation noise
cards.causal_path: High-dimensional stratification (>=15 strata) -> Small calibration n per stratum (median n<30) -> Conformal quantile estimation variance inflation (Var(q_hat) ~ 1/n) -> Stratum-specific coverage variance > (0.05)^2 -> Apparent coverage instability across segments
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage instability reflects true physiological differences in predictability across strata, not estimation noise
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage variance across strata exceeds binomial sampling variance even when calibration n per stratum >100
cards.distinguishing_test: Subsample calibration sets to vary n_per_stratum; mechanism predicts coverage variance scales as 1/n
cards.effect_size_rationale: Conformal quantile variance ~ p(1-p)/n * (1/f(q)^2); at n=20, coverage std dev ~5-8%; at n=100, ~2-3%; physiological predictability differences typically cause <5% coverage spread
minimum_data_needed: Multiple random splits for variance estimation
cards.testable_prediction: Stratum coverage variance inversely proportional to calibration n per stratum (slope ~ -1 on log-log); at n>100 per stratum, coverage variance <0.001
cards.failure_condition: Coverage variance does not decrease with increasing n_per_stratum (slope > -0.5 on log-log)
cards.statistical_test_plan: Simulate subsampling: for each n in [10,20,30,50,100,200], compute coverage variance across strata over 100 random calibration draws; fit log(variance) ~ log(n); test slope = -1
cards.falsification_test: Use conformal prediction with regularization (e.g., smoothed quantile estimation); if coverage variance decreases without increasing n, mechanism confirmed as finite-sample artifact; if variance persists, mechanism falsified
